analyst_view.overall: Hoffenheim (23rd, 4 pts) host Sturm Graz (24th, 4 pts) in a game both need to stay in the play-off race, with Christian Ilzer and Alexander Prass facing their old club. Hoffenheim lost 1-0 at Frankfurt on Saturday but have won their last three home games, scoring eight and conceding one; Gendrey, Hajdari, Hranac and De Cat are out, all on the numbers' list, and Kabak is expected to start. Sturm Graz are six games without a win, three straight defeats, including 2-3 at home to Celje in Europe; Grgic, Khudyakov, Kiteishvili and Rozga are out (all counted) and Paul Koller is a doubt with illness. Portuguese referee Luis Godinho (about 4.5 cards a game) is in charge; with nothing the numbers cannot see, every stat stays where they put it.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals (Hoffenheim 2.1) and already include Hoffenheim's recent form and the defensive absences on their list. Sturm's slump is already in their recent results, and Koller's illness is only a doubt, so nothing points either way and I stay at 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.5 corners, mostly Hoffenheim (7.2), already up a little for Sturm winning corners lately. Hoffenheim should have most of the ball at home, which the split shows, so I stay at 10.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards, already up about 11% for Hoffenheim drawing many bookings from opponents lately and about 5% for referee Luis Godinho (4.5 a game). Ilzer's reunion with his old club adds some edge but there is no sign of bad blood, so I stay at 4.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 32.0 shots, already up about 12% for Hoffenheim's busy recent shooting (103 in six). With Kramaric, Asllani and Lemperle available, I stay at 32.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target, already a little lower for Sturm's recent finishing. Hoffenheim's attack is at full strength and nothing new points either way, so I stay at 9.7.
